claims.assertion: For covered e-commerce and electronic communications, ACM directs providers to publish a readily findable, accessible statement on the website and app.

sources.evidence: ACM explicitly says to place a statement on the website and app describing conformity and make it easy for consumers to find and accessible.

claims.review_note: Existing Yes preserved. Original: 'Op uw website en app plaatst u een verklaring ... Deze verklaring moet eenvoudig vindbaar zijn voor de consument en toegankelijk zijn.' Literal: place a statement on website and app; must be easy to find and accessible. Separate Dutch-to-English agent 2026-09-24: Supported; do not infer that the same placement applies in every sector.

claims.assertion: AFM tells consumer banking and financial e-commerce service providers to prepare an accessibility-statement document, publicly available in writing and orally, without specifying a standalone webpage in the cited passage.

sources.evidence: AFM FAQ says a statement document is required and accessible in writing and orally, e.g. website or brochure and oral request via telephone.

claims.review_note: Original: 'Ja, alle dienstverleners die bankdiensten en e-handelsdiensten verlenen aan consumenten ... De informatie moet schriftelijk en mondeling ter beschikking worden gesteld aan het publiek.' Literal: all consumer banking/e-commerce providers prepare a statement; make information available to public in writing and orally. Isolated language reviewer 2026-09-24: Supported, but only AFM remit is financial e-commerce. This is a separate mode from ACM website placement.

claims.assertion: Conformity information appears in public terms or equivalent documents for covered services, but national sector-specific placement has not been established for every sector in this bounded review.

sources.evidence: AFM provides examples of a website or brochure; does not establish a sector-universal terms/equivalent rule.

claims.review_note: The EAA Annex V sets a terms/equivalent baseline. Verify sector-specific Dutch implementation before asserting identical publication mode for all sectors.

claims.assertion: AFM says consumers may request oral accessibility information by telephone; a general public-on-request-only model is not established.

sources.evidence: AFM says the statement information must be public in writing and orally, oral availability can be requested by telephone.

claims.review_note: Do not recharacterize this as permission to withhold public written information.

claims.assertion: CvdM provides a public form for reporting accessibility complaints about audiovisual media and e-books, with a labeled anonymous option.

sources.evidence: Official page identifies dedicated accessibility route and anonymous option; link redirects to E-loket login inaccessible to tool.

Official accessibility link redirected in an ordinary browser to https://eloket.cvdm.nl/f/5007/login; choosing 'Anoniem invullen' opened https://eloket.cvdm.nl/f/5007/w/anoniem with a visible complaint form. No report was submitted.

claims.review_note: Authority page reachable and correct. Destination https://toegankelijkheid.cvdm.nl/ redirects to https://eloket.cvdm.nl/f/5007/login (reader error). CvdM says DigiD/eHerkenning or anonymous tip possible, but portal usability is unconfirmed. Omitted pending ordinary-browser check. Post-draft ordinary-browser retry 2026-09-24: the CvdM accessibility portal was reachable, showed public complaint instructions and an 'Anoniem invullen' option. Clicking that option opened a visible form with name, email, message and optional attachment fields; it was not submitted. This verifies the entry route and labeled option, not that identifying fields are never requested or that company reporting uses the route. Separate no-history Dutch-to-English reviewer: original snippets 'U kunt ook melding doen over de toegankelijkheid van audiovisuele media en e-boeken', 'Meld toegankelijkheid hier', 'U kunt er ook voor kiezen om anoniem melding te doen', 'Heeft u een klacht over toegankelijkheid?', 'Anoniem invullen'; literal meaning supports 'Public reports: CvdM accessibility form (anonymous option)' and recommends 'Accessibility of audiovisual media and e-books' over the ambiguous 'Audiovisual access'. Final wording rechecked 2026-09-24; verdict supported with that correction.

claims.assertion: ACM accepts English-language company reports from companies outside the Netherlands through its Dutch-only EAA form; ACM does not accept these reports by email.
claims.review_note: Official direct email from ACM senior enforcement officer Hanneke van Rooijen, Toegankelijkheid@acm.nl, 3 December 2025, provided by the contributor in 'Questions about reporting for the EAA (4).eml'. ACM stated form is Dutch-only, companies outside Netherlands may report in English, and email reports are not accepted (the email address is for contact). The contributor asked on 11 December 2025 about publication of a statement, oversight scope, monitoring, warnings, WCAG 2.2 and dark mode; the 24 September 2026 reminder says the questions remain unanswered. Summarized with contributor authorization; raw email, personal phone and private details not published. Reporting form is independently verified at the ACM official URL.
